messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>

Cc:

Subject: Subscription commit matrix + FinOps escalation: Atlas renewal

Team —

Quick context: Atlas HealthTech (renewal due 2026-03-31) is flagging unexpected usage growth and asking for a mid-contract pricing review. Sales has signaled a potential 20% discount request tied to a 24-month extension. Finance needs a crisp impact view on forecast and margin.

What I need by EOD Thu (2/19):
- Updated commit probability per segment for Atlas accounts in our renewal workbook (PS/Platform/Support). Please annotate why you changed any probability.
- Financial delta (net ARR movement and gross margin impact) for the 20% discount scenario vs baseline.
- If an approval path is required, indicate approver and suggested cadence.

I'm attaching the Q1 usage export Atlas shared and the draft matrix I started. Laura — can you confirm current contract baseline? Naomi — can you run a quick margin calc and flag whether this requires Finance escalation to Legal/SalesOps? Marissa — can you prepare a short note for the CRO with recommended next steps if we need to approve the discount?

Thanks,

David Kim
Sr. Account Executive, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Q1_Usage_Summary.pdf (summary, 2 pages)
Attachment: Proposed_Matrix.xlsx (workbook, 3 sheets)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: david_kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subscription commit matrix + FinOps escalation: Atlas renewal

David —

Thanks for pulling this together. I pulled the signed AMS and the last two quarters of seat/consumption baselines. Quick notes inline: 
- Baseline ARR (as-billed): $1.2M annualized; committed seats 80; overage billing has been in place but historically under 5% of total.
- The proposed 20% list discount applied across Platform would reduce billed ARR to ~$960k on a straight-line basis but Atlas is asking to cap overage at current levels which increases risk to unit economics.

I'll update the commit probabilities in the workbook: my preliminary view is move Forecast -> Commit for the Platform line (from 65% to 85%) if Atlas signs 24 months and removes auto-escalation. I'll mark Professional Services as Probable (40%) pending SOW pricing confirmation.

Forwarding the signed AMS in case Naomi needs it for margin math.

Laura Bennett
Director, Accounts 
Redwood Inference

David / Team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Atlas is open to a 24-month extension but we need unit cost certainty: the recent uptick in usage is real (see Q1 export) and our board wants a predictable invoice profile. Key asks from us: 
- A blended unit price that caps overage above current Q1 levels.
- A commensurate discount for committing to 24 months and a commit floor.
- 60-day runway for our procurement to get internal approvals; meanwhile our finance team asked for a modeled invoice schedule.

I attached a proposed pricing matrix (Proposed_Matrix.xlsx) that shows the blended price we had in mind and an invoice cadence. Let us know what flexibility there is on contract language for capping overages.

—Avery Collins
Sr. Procurement Manager
Atlas HealthTech

Subject: Re: Subscription commit matrix + FinOps escalation: Atlas renewal — Finance stances and next steps

Team —

I ran the numbers and summarized impacts; highlights below (detailed sheet attached to internal workbook):
- Baseline ARR: $1.2M.
- Scenario (20% across-platform discount, 24-month commit, cap overage at Q1 levels): Estimated billed ARR year 1 = $980k (blended after overage assumptions); gross margin impact ~ -6 percentage points driven by support and platform variable costs.
- Break-even threshold (for Finance sign-off without CRO approval) would require either: a) discount < 12% or b) guaranteed minimum commit of 30% higher than current floor.

Recommendations / action items:
1) Update Salesforce commit probability for Platform -> 85% and PS -> 40%. Mark reason as: "24-mo extension in negotiation; pricing contingent on overage cap."
2) Escalate to Legal & SalesOps if Sales wants >15% discount OR if Atlas demands a hard overage cap in contract language. That path requires CRO and Legal lead review (anticipated 3–5 business days).
3) Marissa to draft a 1-page executive brief for CRO summarizing tradeoffs and recommended approval (I can supply the financial appendix).

I'll attach the internal margin worksheet in the HubSpot record and link FIN-482 for tracking. If we need a faster answer to preserve the deal, recommend we present a two-option approval to CRO: 12% discount w/ soft cap OR 20% discount w/ stricter commit and Legal review.

Naomi Feldman
Lead Financial Analyst, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
